rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-3 report a two-year field study (2018-2019) on commercial potato fields in New Mexico with Sentek capacitance probes, soil water balance ET, FAO-56 ET and OpenET satellite ET.
rows.notes: The study reports no tuber yield data at all and has no control (non-sensor) plots; all fields were scheduled with soil moisture sensors. The claimed 6.6% yield increase versus control plots does not appear anywhere in the paper. The study's own results concern soil water dynamics by depth, the effective rooting zone (upper 40 cm), and seasonal ET estimates (580-645 mm by water balance) compared across three methods.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-3 report own field measurements of soil water at six depths with Sentek probes across five (2018) and four (2019) commercial potato fields, applied irrigation amounts (Figure 8) and ET estimates by three methods.
rows.notes: The study reports applied irrigation (777 <U+00B1> 36 mm seasonal average) under sensor-based scheduling but has no comparison with a non-sensor control, no measured water saving, no farmer survey, and no 15% reduction figure; the abstract's statement that probe-based scheduling improved irrigation water use is an assertion, not a measured result. Its actual findings (effective rooting zone of 40 cm, little water extraction below 40 cm, ET comparisons) are at most a precondition for better scheduling rather than evidence of water savings.

notes: Full text appears complete. The paper is a primary field study on soil water dynamics, rooting zone and ET of sprinkler-irrigated potato; it contains no yield data, no control treatment and no farmer-reported outcomes, so it does not support the specific figures (6.6% yield increase, 15% water reduction) attributed to it in the passage.
